research_profile.primary_taxonomy: Machine Learning Systems and Hardware-Aware Optimization
research_profile.core_contribution: Ph.D. researcher and machine learning systems engineer with expertise in hardware-aware optimization of neural networks for embedded and edge systems, including pruning, quantization, sparse training, compiler-level model transformations, and resource-constrained AI deployment. Research spans edge inference systems, embedded AI, ONNX-based model transformation workflows, and reproducible evaluation pipelines for efficient learning systems. Current research interest: extending hardware-aware inference optimization techniques toward energy-efficient on-device training and training-accelerator design.

Machine learning systems and hardware-software co-design
Model compression: pruning, quantization, and dynamic/sparse training
Hardware-aware inference and compiler-level model transformations (ONNX, IR rewrites)
Embedded AI, edge computing, and resource-constrained architectures

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Unstructured Pruning for Multi-Layer Perceptrons with Tanh Activation
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: For Multi-layer Perceptrons (MLPs) with tanh activation function, we propose an effective unstructured pruning technique that removes redundant neurons while preserving accuracy. The method targets neurons with activations clustered near -1, 0, or 1, leveraging the zero-centered properties of tanh, and achieved neuron count reductions of 36.8% for MNIST models and up to 72% for a breast cancer dataset with minimal accuracy loss.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Neuron-level pruning methodology tailored to tanh activation functions; demonstrates activation-aware weight thresholding

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: A Distributed Framework for Real-Time Object Detection at Low Frame Rates with IoT Edge Nodes
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: This work develops a framework for efficient object detection on a distributed, constrained platform system, using the PYNQ Z1 AP-SoC as the IoT edge node platform integrated with state-of-the-art object detection algorithms. The team achieved 19.23 frames per second with three IoT nodes using a Binarized Neural Network (BNN) image classification algorithm, with the frame rate scaling directly with the number of nodes in the network.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: End-to-end system for distributed inference across heterogeneous edge devices; addresses latency and bandwidth constraints

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Range Based Hardware Optimization of Multi-Layer Perceptrons with ReLUs
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: To address severely constrained hardware platforms, this paper proposes a range-based optimization approach for MLPs using ReLU activations.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Hardware-aware quantization bounds for ReLU networks; static range analysis for FPGA/ASIC implementation

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Sigmoid-Based Neuron Pruning Technique for MLPs on IoT Edge Devices
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel sigmoid-based neuron pruning technique specifically designed for deploying MLPs on IoT edge devices.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Activation-specific pruning heuristics for sigmoid functions; memory-efficient inference on edge MCUs

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Layer-Wise Filter Thresholding Based CNN Pruning for Efficient IoT Edge Implementations
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for efficiently running convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on Internet of Things (IoT) edge devices. The proposed method utilizes threshold-based pruning to optimize pre-trained CNN models, enabling inference on resource-constrained IoT and edge devices. The pruning thresholds for each layer are iteratively adjusted using a range-based threshold pruning technique. The pre-trained network evaluates the accuracy of the pruned model and dynamically adjusts the pruning thresholds to maximize accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated on the widely-used LeNet benchmark network, with MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN datasets. Our experimental results show that for the MNIST dataset, we can prune 62-64% of weights for an accuracy loss of 1-4%. Similarly, for Fashion-MNIST, we can prune around 64% for an accuracy loss of around 2.92%, and for the SVHN dataset, we can prune around 55% of weights for an accuracy loss of 1.7% on average, saving resources.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Structured pruning via layer-wise filter selection; demonstrates scalable CNN compression for IoT deployments

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Simulated Annealing Based Integerization of Hidden Weights for Area-Efficient IoT Edge Intelligence
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: Neural network (NN) model accuracy has dramatically increased as a result of the usage of extreme parameterization. However, this comes with significant overheads, including increased area, energy consumption, higher memory, and latency. The deployment of these highly parameterized NN models is becoming a challenge in resource-constrained environments. We present a proof-of-concept methodology to address this problem. We proposed a novel approach based on Simulated Annealing (SA) for NN model optimization for designing efficient hardware for Internet-of-Things (IoT) edge intelligent devices. The SA algorithm is used to optimize a given NN model generated with a standard learning framework. It improves the pre-trained NN model by perturbing a specific amount of hidden layer neuron weights by rounding off some of the weights that are close to integers without compromising the model's accuracy. As a result of rounding, some weights may end up with zero value leading to model pruning. We validated the approach with three MLP classification benchmarks synthesized with Xilinx Vivado (v.2019.2). We assume all floating point weights are stored in IEEE 754 FP32 format. We performed three different SA runs with a constant temperature reduction rate (alpha) of 0.95 and a number of iterations (n) of 100, 1,000, and 10,000, respectively. In experiments I, II, and III, we achieve average flip-flop savings of 20.38%, 22.93%, and 24.45% and LUT savings of 21.43%, 23.84%, and 25.51% respectively.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Integer weight conversion via simulated annealing; reduces hardware area for ASIC/FPGA implementations without retraining

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Simulated Annealing Based Area Optimization of Multilayer Perceptron Hardware for IoT Edge Devices
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: Highly parameterized Neural Network (NN) models are difficult to deploy on resource-constrained hardware platforms due to their large size, expensive computational costs, and high memory requirements. There is a need for area efficient NN models without compromising model accuracy. We propose Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm based NN optimization to generate area-optimized hardware for multilayer perceptrons. In the SA loop, we aim to change hidden layer weights to integer values, in two steps: (1) A random subset of the hidden weights are perturbed by an amount proportional to the SA temperature; (2) the new weights that are proximate to integers are rounded which will help reduce the hardware due to operation strength reduction (for example, multiply by a power of 2 reduces to shift operation). Throughout the optimization, we prefer SA moves that do not sacrifice the model's efficiency. We validate the proposed methodology on five MLP benchmarks (the number of model parameters varies from 35 to 528) implemented on FPGA. We observe the best case savings are obtained for all five NN's when the amount of perturbation (p) is 10% and the number of perturbations at each temperature (N) is 10,000 keeping constant temperature reduction function (alpha) at 0.95. For the best case solution, the average savings in LUTs and FFs are 24.83% and 25.76%, respectively with an average model accuracy degradation of 1.64%.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Area optimization via simulated annealing for MLP hardware implementations; demonstrates resource-efficient IoT deployment

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Area Efficient VLSI ASIC Implementation of Multilayer Perceptrons
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: This paper proposes a simulated annealing (SA)-based neural network optimization approach for designing an area- and power-efficient hardware model for MLPs, targeting hidden layer neuron weights for optimization to integer values. Perturbations proportional to the annealing temperature push weights toward the nearest integer, and register resizing plus operator strength reduction further minimize hardware footprint, achieving average savings of 27.53% area, 27.28% power, and 27.71% flip-flops with only a 2.74% average accuracy degradation.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: ASIC implementation of optimized MLPs; demonstrates area-efficient neural network hardware deployment

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Automated Hidden Neuron Optimization for Multilayer Perceptrons for Classification Tasks
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: This study presents a novel approach combining preprocessing, feature selection, and strategic MLP architecture design to address the challenge of determining the optimal number of hidden neurons in an MLP network for classification tasks.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Automated neuron selection methodology for MLP classification tasks; demonstrates performance optimization techniques

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Comprehensive Benchmarking of Activation-Aware Structured Pruning for MCU Deployment: An Empirical Evaluation Study
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: Neural network deployment on microcontrollers faces severe memory constraints, with even modest MLPs exceeding the 2KB SRAM limit of popular platforms like Arduino Nano RP2040. While pruning techniques can reduce model size, existing approaches apply uniform strategies regardless of activation function characteristics, missing optimization opportunities specific to each activation type. We present a systematic benchmarking study of activation-aware structured pruning that evaluates deployment effectiveness across 9 tabular datasets, 3 activation functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh), and 2 MCU platforms (Arduino Nano RP2040, NodeMCU ESP8266) using correlation-based pruning with activation-specific thresholds. Our evaluation demonstrates 100% deployment success across all 54 configurations, with Arduino RP2040 achieving 33.1% average speed improvement and NodeMCU ESP8266 showing 16.5% memory reduction while maintaining accuracy within +/-0.7%. Activation-specific analysis reveals ReLU models achieve best speed performance (up to 65% speedup), Sigmoid models show highest memory compression (up to 73% reduction), and Tanh provides balanced characteristics. This work provides the first comprehensive empirical validation of activation-aware pruning on actual microcontroller platforms, enabling practitioners to make informed optimization decisions for resource-constrained deployments.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Real MCU deployment validation with significant speedup and memory savings; provides practical guidelines for activation-aware pruning

peer_reviewed_conferences.title: Dynamic Sparse Training and Compression Pipeline for Deployment-Ready CNNs
peer_reviewed_conferences.abstract: Convolutional neural networks achieve state-of-the-art computer vision performance but face deployment challenges on resource-constrained edge devices due to high computational and memory requirements. Existing pruning methods often trade accuracy for efficiency or lack integration with deployment pipelines, limiting real-world applicability. We propose a dynamic sparse training framework that integrates Grad-CAM-guided feature pruning with RigL-inspired adaptive sparsity updates, creating a pipeline from training to deployment-ready models. Our approach prunes low-importance features while dynamically adjusting sparsity levels based on validation performance, enabling high compression rates without accuracy degradation. On LeNet-5 (MNIST), we achieve 98.98% sparsity with 98.94% accuracy, reducing model size from 1.65MB to 0.42MB (74.5% reduction) and achieving 3.8x inference speedup. On VGG-11 (CIFAR-10), we achieve 89.85% sparsity with 88.28% accuracy (+0.62% improvement), reducing model size from 107.37MB to 26.89MB (75% reduction) with 8.16x GPU speedup. Our framework provides a complete training-to-deployment pipeline with operator fusion, quantization, and ONNX export.
peer_reviewed_conferences.contribution: Novel combination of Grad-CAM-guided pruning and dynamic sparsity; complete training-to-deployment pipeline with strong compression and speedup results
reviewer_highlights: Novel combination of Grad-CAM-guided pruning and dynamic sparsity
